verses.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, to God's holy people in Ephesus, the faithful in Christ Jesus:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Praise the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! In Christ, he has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in heaven.
Before the world began, he chose us in Christ to be holy and blameless before him, living in love.
God decided in advance to adopt us as his children through Jesus Christ. This pleased him and was what he wanted.
So we praise the glory of his grace, which he freely gave us in the one he loves.
Through Christ's blood we are set free, and our sins are forgiven, in keeping with the riches of God's grace.
He poured that grace out on us, along with all wisdom and understanding.
God made known to us the mystery of his will, in line with his good purpose, which he planned in Christ:
to bring everything together under Christ when the right time comes—everything in heaven and on earth.
In Christ we were also chosen to receive an inheritance, as God had planned in advance, since he carries out everything according to his will.
His purpose was that we, who were the first to put our hope in Christ, would live to praise his glory.
You also heard the true message, the Good News that saves you, and believed in Christ. Then God marked you as his own by giving you the promised Holy Spirit.
The Spirit is the guarantee of our inheritance until God redeems his own people, to the praise of his glory.
That's why, since I heard about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all God's people,
I haven't stopped thanking God for you and remembering you in my prayers.
I pray that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the glorious Father, will give you the Spirit of wisdom and revelation so you can know him better.
I pray that the eyes of your heart will be enlightened, so you'll know the hope of his calling, the riches of his glorious inheritance among his people,
and the immeasurable greatness of his power toward us who believe. That power works with the same mighty strength
God used in Christ when he raised him from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavenly realms,
far above every ruler, authority, power, and lord, and every name that can be named—not only in this age but also in the age to come.
God placed everything under Christ's feet and appointed him as head over everything for the church,
which is his body, the fullness of the one who fills everything in every way.
